ASRS & High-Density Shuttle Systems

Overview

How it works

Automated storage and retrieval systems can bring together storage racks, shuttles, cranes, conveyors, control software and safety systems. Equipment selection follows the required load profile, SKU mix, throughput, site geometry and operational integration needs.

Typical applications

  • High-throughput distribution
  • Automated pallet warehousing
  • Tote and parts order fulfilment

Configurations

ASRS configurations

Pallet shuttle

A shuttle typically moves loads inside rack lanes or across defined tracks, suited to dense storage of palletised goods.

Stacker crane ASRS

A stacker crane travels along aisles to access storage positions, placing and retrieving loads under controlled motion.

Mini-load ASRS

Mini-load systems are generally intended for smaller loads such as bins, totes or cartons rather than full pallets.

Designs, payloads and interfaces vary by vendor and are confirmed for each project from the actual equipment model and operating assumptions.

Engineering

Design considerations

Load types
Pallets, totes or cases; vendor and system dependent.
Payload
Specified for each selected machine and load-handling device.
Throughput
Calculated from cycle time, travel distances, demand and system layout.
Space utilisation
Determined by layout, unit-load geometry and maintenance access.
Controls and safety
PLC, WMS/WCS integration and protective systems as required.

Technical specifications are design considerations, not fixed certified performance values. Confirm claims with engineering and supplier data before deployment.

FAQs

Common questions

What does ASRS mean?

ASRS stands for Automated Storage and Retrieval System, a combination of storage structures and controlled machines that place and retrieve goods.

How does a pallet shuttle differ from a stacker crane?

A shuttle typically moves loads inside rack lanes or across defined tracks, while a stacker crane travels along aisles to access storage positions. Designs and interfaces vary by vendor.

What is a mini-load ASRS?

Mini-load systems are generally intended for smaller loads such as bins, totes or cartons rather than full pallets.

How are payload and throughput determined?

They are calculated from an actual equipment model, storage geometry, travel cycle, lift motion, traffic and operating assumptions. Generic vendor examples cannot be used as ProRack specifications.
